rejection_findings.finding: This prose is supportable, but submission 0034 could not be partially accepted because its paired comm_laws_0012 revision was defective.
The prose conflates the 30-60 Dionysian singing chorus with later myth-tellers who can no longer bear songs; separate those age groups and cite each claim precisely.

revisions.title: Education teaches the pleasure of the beautiful
revisions.body: The Athenian defines education through choral practice: song and dance are its parts, but bodily performance is not enough. The sharper criterion is whether pleasure and dislike are correctly trained toward the beautiful and shameful; the exchange then compresses this provisional account to keep the inquiry moving.

revisions.title: Age separates the singing choruses from myth-telling
revisions.body: The Sidonian story is marked as improbable but useful as a paradigm for legislation. The Athenian then separates the choruses by age: children and men up to thirty sing in the first two, while men over thirty through sixty form a third singing group later discussed as a chorus of Dionysus. Only after that singing range does he assign those who can no longer bear songs to myth-telling about the same ethical matters. Wine is then proposed for those from forty onward as a remedy for old age's harshness, making participation in song less shameful and more willing.
